The 75 bp hike to 3.75–4% and continued balance-sheet runoff keep policy clearly restrictive and inflation-focused. However, the FSR around this period flags tighter financial conditions, reduced Treasury market depth, elevated rate volatility, and vulnerabilities at some nonbank intermediaries and bond funds, alongside cooling but still-stretched housing valuations. These stability considerations reinforce the Committee’s new emphasis on “cumulative tightening” and policy lags, implying more caution on the pace of future increases even as inflation risks remain paramount. Net takeaway: hawkish but increasingly risk-aware and data-dependent.
